paper_title: I Don't Know Explicit Modeling of Uncertainty with an [IDK] Token

model_annotation: The plot illustrates the tradeoff between IDK recall and IDK error rate for different parameter configurations, with each data point annotated with its corresponding value. The x-axis represents the IDK error rate, ranging from 0.0 to 0.25 on a linear scale, while the y-axis shows the IDK recall, ranging from 0.1 to 0.7. Four distinct lines are plotted: a solid blue line labeled "No $\mathcal{L}_{\text{FP-reg}}$, fixed $\lambda$", a dashed green line labeled "No $\mathcal{L}_{\text{FP-reg}}$, adaptive $\lambda$", a solid orange line labeled "With $\mathcal{L}_{\text{FP-reg}}$, fixed $\lambda$", and a dashed red line labeled "With $\mathcal{L}_{\text{FP-reg}}$, adaptive $\lambda$". The blue line starts at (0.02, 0.1) and increases to (0.25, 0.65), with data points annotated at 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6. The green line starts at (0.05, 0.2) and increases to (0.25, 0.65), with data points annotated at 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5. The orange line starts at (0.02, 0.1) and increases to (0.25, 0.65), with data points annotated at 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5. The red line starts at (0.02, 0.2) and increases to (0.25, 0.65), with data points annotated at 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5. All lines show a general increasing trend, indicating that higher IDK recall is associated with higher IDK error rates across all configurations.
